title: Nuevo Laredo's Catrina contest celebrates tradition as Día de Muertos approaches Nov. 1
excerpt: Nuevo Laredo opened its 2026 Catrina and Catrín contest as part of the city's Día de Muertos season, with 30,000 pesos in prizes, as the Nov. 1-2 observance approaches.
content:
Nuevo Laredo's municipal government opened its 2026 Catrina and Catrín contest as part of the city's Día de Muertos season, inviting residents to turn tradition, makeup and costume into a public celebration of Mexican identity as the Nov. 1-2 observance approaches.

The contest, organized through the city's Education, Culture and Sports Secretariat and its Art and Culture Directorate, rewards creativity and fidelity to Day of the Dead traditions, according to municipal announcements carried by local outlets. Registration took place at Estación Palabra “Gabriel García Márquez,” at Avenida César López de Lara 1020 in Colonia Centro, weekdays from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., with information available at 867 713 4746.

Prizes and judging

The contest carries 30,000 pesos in total prizes: 15,000 pesos for first place, 10,000 for second and 5,000 for third, paid later by bank transfer once winners submit the required tax and banking documents, local reports said.

A jury named by the Art and Culture Directorate judges creativity and originality, makeup and quality of characterization, stage presence during the presentation and walk, and the use of elements of Tamaulipas identity, such as its traditions, heritage, historic figures and cultural expressions. Municipal employees and DIF Municipal workers were not eligible to enter.

Cemeteries ready for 20,000 to 25,000 visitors

The contest is only one part of the city's Day of the Dead preparations. Nuevo Laredo's municipal cemeteries, the Panteón Antiguo and the Panteón del Sur, are ready to receive an estimated 20,000 to 25,000 visitors, after cleaning, maintenance, lighting and security work ordered by Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal, local reports said.

Even Arredondo Bravo, secretary of Primary Public Services, said both cemeteries are prepared after year-round conservation work plus seasonal decoration, lighting, water trucks and emergency power plants. Municipal crews also cleared weeds, removed waste, cleaned common areas and checked headstones and structures that could pose a risk to visitors.

Security will be reinforced with Municipal Guard patrols, coordinated with state police and federal agencies, with special attention at night. The cemeteries open at 8 a.m., with institutional closing planned between 9 p.m. and 10 p.m., though officials said consideration is given to families who traditionally stay longer.

For families on both sides of the border, the season is a shared one: Laredo's own Día de Muertos events continue into November, and Nuevo Laredo's contest and cemetery preparations show the same tradition taking public form across the river, in costume, in cemeteries and in the civic calendar itself.
